profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Backblaze Cloud Storage & Backup
profile.summary:
I've spent most of the past ten years working on cloud-based network security products. I'm interested in solving problems around scalability and concurrency, and generally learning new and challenging things.

Specialties: C, C++, SMTP, Java

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Worked on account management and billing: auditing, reconciliation, security and compliance, etc.  Wrote Java code to integrate our billing system with the Stripe payment gateway and other third-party services.  Worked on transition from in-house billing system to Orb.  Worked on implementation of group billing for both B2B and B2C customers.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description:
Led development relating to the SMTP proxy, MTA, and other SMTP-related components of SonicWall Email Security products.  Designed and implemented Email Continuity, G Suite integration, URL harvesting, and other features.  Led the design and implementation of Time-Of-Click URL protection (ToC) across several distributed teams.  

Designed a RESTful API for ToC to allow URL information to be communicated from Mail User Agents to ToC servers, and for aggregated information to be communicated from ToC servers to Email Security Control Centers for diagnostics and reporting.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on the SMTP proxy and MTA components of Email Security products. My biggest project during that time has been designing and building multitenant clusters for the Hosted Email Security product we created. My SMTP-related work included implementing recipient-based path selection, sender-based path selection, Office 365 integration, support for Capture (sandboxing), connection management, designing a spooling server, etc. I also continued to develop features for the standalone product, such as customizable DSN, per-domain TLS, and support for SMTP AUTH.

Did a major rewrite of the SMTP monitoring system, improving scalability and improving performance by an order of magnitude. Did a major rewrite of our thread library to fix API deficiencies, memory leaks, and other design flaws. I've continued to make enhancements to our CASS product, such as adding address books. In addition to SMTP code, I do a lot of work on issues involving concurrency, scalability, and the overall design and architecture of our products.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on the SMTP proxy and MTA components of SonicWALL Email Security.

Helped develop CASS product, a collaborative effort between the Email Security team and the UTM team in which email passing through the UTM is routed through the CASS Cloud for threat analysis. Email is optionally routed to a CASS Junkstore for further processing.

Used C++ and Java to develop new features and improve existing functionality for several releases of SonicWALL Email Security on Windows and Linux. Used Berkeley Database for collaborative spam and virus blocking. Rewrote portions of the junk notifier subsystem to improve robustness and serviceability. Used zlib to write code that downloads malware thumbprints via compressed streams. Rewrote portions of base and utility classes to improve performance and prevent resource exhaustion. Rewrote logging system to provide finer-grained control over logging and more useful diagnostic information. Rewrote the Wise installer.

Helped port MailFrontier's software product to run on a SonicWALL appliance and added new appliance-specific functionality. Led rebranding/conversion effort.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
MailFrontier was an email security company (blocked spam, virus, fraud/phishing, policy violations, DHA, DoS attacks, etc). 

Used C++ and Java to develop new features and improve existing functionality for several major releases and numerous point releases of MailFrontier Enterprise Gateway on Windows, Linux, and Solaris. Integrated Firebird database into core product for reporting. Wrote C++ code to parse email records and populate the database, and to query the database for metrics. Used Apache Tomcat, Struts, JDBC, and JFreeChart to produce reports. Wrote JSP/servlets for numerous UI features and wrote C++ code to implement the infrastructure. Wrote documentation and guides for the last major release. Led internationalization/localization effort.

positions.title: Staff Engineer
positions.description:
Developed new features for and did code maintenance of the Advanced Window Toolkit (AWT), the first GUI toolkit for the Java Development Kit (JDK).  AWT widgets are based on native win32 and motif widgets.  The AWT contains the native (X-Windows and win32) and Java event architecture upon which the Swing toolkit and other client technologies are based.  

Worked on a dozen or so releases of the Java Software Development Kit (JDK 1.1.5 through 1.5.0).  Primarily responsible for key events, text widgets, and painting.  Redesigned key event and painting subsystems to work on various Solaris, Linux, and Microsoft Windows platforms.  Performance lead for AWT.  

AWT Lead Engineer for several releases (JDK 1.3 through 1.4.2).  Responsible for planning new features and targeted bug lists, tracking and driving progress towards team goals, and working with other groups and customers.  Manager of the AWT group (2001-2002).  Managed sixteen geographically distributed employees and contractors in two groups (AWT and Drag&Drop).  Responsible for hiring, performance reviews, etc.
